blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY — The summer capital is moving closer to raising the minimum legal drinking age from 18 to 21 to curb alcohol-related harm among young people despite concerns from bar operators over the proposed restriction’s impact on the city’s nightlife industry. The city council last week approved on second reading the proposed Alcohol Harm Prevention Ordinance (Proposed Ordinance No. 0023-20), which seeks to tighten regulations on the sale and serving of alcoholic beverages, including stricter liquor licensing requirements.
